You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

1: From: Thomas Orr <torr@hargravestein.com>
2: To: Priya Nagarajan <pnagarajan@hargravestein.com>
3: Date: Tue, 06 May 2025 08:47:00 -0000
4: Subject: FW: Ironbridge ACA – Bank Turn 1 / Instructions for Counter-Turn
5:  [Matter No. 2025-HSC-04417]
6: Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
7: Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable

9: 
10: Priya,
11: 
12: Forwarding below the transmittal from Lena Marchetti and Reginald Stowe at Bl=
13: ackmere Fox (received yesterday afternoon) along with their redline of our Pi=
14: nnacle form ACA =E2=80=94 this is Bank Turn 1 (Blackmere Fox matter ref. BF-I=
15: RB-25-00893). I've reviewed the markup. Here's what I need from you and how I=
16: 'd like you to approach the counter-turn.
17: 
18: **Background**
19: 
20: This is the Account Control Agreement for the three Graycliff Industries, Inc=
21: . deposit accounts held at Ironbridge National Bank, N.A. (OCC Charter No. 18=
22: 742):
23: 
24: - Operating Account (=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F-4471)
25: - Payroll Account (=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F-4472)
26: - Collections Account (=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F=E2=97=8F-4473)
27: 
28: Parties are Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC (Secured Party), Graycliff Industr=
29: ies, Inc. (Depositor), and Ironbridge National Bank, N.A. (Depository Bank). =
30: The ACA is required under Section 6.14(b) of the Credit Agreement dated April=
31:  14, 2025 (maturing April 14, 2030), in connection with the $175MM revolving =
32: credit facility.
33: 
34: **Deliverables**
35: 
36: I need two things from you:
37: 
38: 1. **Lender Turn 2 redline** =E2=80=94 our counter-markup of the Bank's Turn =
39: 1.
40: 2. **Cover note/transmittal letter** to Blackmere Fox (addressed to Marchetti=
41:  and Stowe) walking through Pinnacle's positions on each of the Bank's 13 sub=
42: stantive changes.
43: 
44: **Both due to me for review by end of day Friday, May 9.**
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: **PERFECTION DEADLINE**
49: 
50: Keep this front and center: Section 6.14(b) requires delivery of the executed=
51:  ACA, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Age=
52: nt, by **May 30, 2025**. That's 46 calendar days from the Credit Agreement da=
53: te and roughly 24 days from today. We need to close out or substantially narr=
54: ow open issues in this turn =E2=80=94 we cannot afford extended back-and-fort=
55: h. UCC control over these deposit accounts must be perfected by that deadline=
56:  to maintain valid security interests. Every round we add eats into that wind=
57: ow.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: **CLIENT PRIORITIES**
62: 
63: I've spoken with Diana Whitford (VP =E2=80=93 Portfolio Management, Pinnacle)=
64:  several times over the past week. Her priorities, in order:
65: 
66: 1. **Strong, reliable control mechanics.** The ACA must give Pinnacle enforce=
67: able control over the deposit accounts once exclusive control is triggered. N=
68: o carve-outs or conditions that undercut that.
69: 2. **Resist the Bank's liability cap.** The aggregate balances across the thr=
70: ee accounts are approximately **$38,150,000** (Operating ~$22.35M, Payroll ~$=
71: 4.18M, Collections ~$11.62M). The Bank's proposed $50,000 cap is not remotely=
72:  proportionate.
73: 3. **New York governing law.**
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: **ISSUE-BY-ISSUE DIRECTION**
78: 
79: Address all 13 substantive changes in both the redline and the cover note. He=
80: re's my guidance:
81: 
82: **(a) Entitlement Order vs. Instruction Language (Bank's =C2=A7 2(a))**
83: 
84: The Bank substituted "instruction" for "entitlement order" throughout =C2=A7 =
85: 2(a). Our form deliberately uses "entitlement order" language consistent with=
86:  UCC Article 8.
87: 
88: **Non-negotiable.** Restore "entitlement order" throughout. The cover note sh=
89: ould explain this is necessary to ensure UCC Article 8 control and proper per=
90: fection. Don't leave room for ambiguity on this one.
91: 
92: **(b) Springing Exclusive Control / Account Operation Carve-Out (Bank's marku=
93: p to =C2=A7 2)**
94: 
95: Our form provides for springing exclusive control upon default. The Bank's ma=
96: rkup adds a carve-out allowing Graycliff to continue operating the accounts w=
97: ithout Secured Party consent until delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control =
98: (NOEC).
99: 
100: **Non-negotiable on the springing structure itself.** We can accept =E2=80=94=
101:  and our form already contemplates =E2=80=94 that Graycliff operates the acco=
102: unts in the ordinary course prior to NOEC delivery. But the Bank's carve-out =
103: language as drafted could undercut the effectiveness of exclusive control onc=
104: e an NOEC is delivered. Tighten the language so that (i) pre-NOEC ordinary co=
105: urse operation is clearly permitted, but (ii) upon delivery of an NOEC, Grayc=
106: liff's access is cut off without qualification. Make that distinction crisp.
107: 
108: **(c) Conflicting Instructions Waterfall / Bank Set-Off Priority (Bank's =C2=
109: =A7 3)**
110: 
111: The Bank's markup gives Bank set-off rights priority over Secured Party instr=
112: uctions in the conflicting-instructions waterfall.
113: 
114: **Resist.** Secured Party instructions must prevail. Cite the UCC control fra=
115: mework in the cover note =E2=80=94 the whole point of a control agreement is =
116: that the secured party's instructions override.
117: 
118: **(d) Set-Off Scope (Bank's =C2=A7 4)**
119: 
120: The Bank's markup permits set-off for "any obligation owed to Bank by Deposit=
121: or, whether direct or contingent."
122: 
123: **Some compromise is acceptable here.** We can live with a narrower set-off c=
124: arve-out limited to direct, matured, liquidated obligations arising under the=
125:  deposit account agreements themselves =E2=80=94 but exclude contingent oblig=
126: ations, derivatives exposures, and affiliate obligations. Draft the narrower =
127: formulation and flag it in the cover note as a good-faith accommodation. This=
128:  is an area where showing flexibility will serve us.
129: 
130: **(e) NOEC Compliance Period (Bank's =C2=A7 5)**
131: 
132: Our form says 2 business days; the Bank marked it up to 5.
133: 
134: **Counter at 3 business days.** That is the maximum the client will accept. F=
135: rame it as a reasonable middle ground in the cover note.
136: 
137: **(f) Indemnification / Gross Negligence (Bank's =C2=A7 6)**
138: 
139: The Bank's markup extends the indemnification obligation to cover the Bank's =
140: own gross negligence.
141: 
142: **Non-negotiable.** Reject this. Standard market practice does not require a =
143: secured party to indemnify a depository bank for the bank's own gross neglige=
144: nce. Restore the carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct. The c=
145: over note should be direct on this =E2=80=94 cite market practice.
146: 
147: **(g) Aggregate Liability Cap (Bank's =C2=A7 7(a))**
148: 
149: The Bank inserted a $50,000 aggregate liability cap.
150: 
151: **Non-negotiable in its current form.** As noted above, total controlled depo=
152: sits are approximately $38.15 million. A $50,000 cap is absurd and effectivel=
153: y eliminates any meaningful accountability. In the redline, delete the cap en=
154: tirely. As a fallback position (do not put this in the cover note =E2=80=94 t=
155: his is for our internal negotiation only), we could propose tying the cap to =
156: a percentage of or the actual aggregate balances in the controlled accounts. =
157: The cover note should make clear that $50,000 is unacceptable and explain why.
158: 
159: **(h) Consequential Damages Waiver (Bank's =C2=A7 7(b))**
160: 
161: The Bank inserted a mutual waiver of consequential, punitive, and indirect da=
162: mages.
163: 
164: Flag for discussion in the cover note but treat as lower priority given the o=
165: ther =C2=A7 7 issues. If we secure deletion or meaningful revision of the lia=
166: bility cap, a mutual consequential damages waiver becomes more palatable. Not=
167: e our reservation of rights to revisit but don't die on this hill in this tur=
168: n.
169: 
170: **(i) Set-Off Lookback / Subordination of Bank Lien (Bank's =C2=A7 8)**
171: 
172: Our form provides for full subordination of Bank liens. The Bank's markup lim=
173: its the subordination with a 90-day lookback cap.
174: 
175: **Resist at 90 days.** The client-directed minimum acceptable lookback is **1=
176: 80 days**. Counter at 180 days and explain in the cover note that anything le=
177: ss creates a gap in the subordination protection that is unacceptable to the =
178: Secured Party.
179: 
180: **(j) Termination Rights (Bank's =C2=A7 9)**
181: 
182: Our form requires Secured Party consent for termination. The Bank's markup gi=
183: ves the Bank a unilateral right to terminate on 30 days' notice.
184: 
185: **Resist unilateral termination.** As a fallback, propose a minimum of **90 d=
186: ays' written notice** with an express right for the Secured Party to transiti=
187: on the accounts to a replacement depository bank during the notice period. Th=
188: e cover note should emphasize that abrupt termination could impair perfection=
189:  of the security interest.
190: 
191: **(k) Governing Law (Bank's change)**
192: 
193: Our form specifies New York. The Bank changed to North Carolina.
194: 
195: **Push for New York in this turn.** Present it as firm in the cover note. (Be=
196: tween us =E2=80=94 this may ultimately be a concession if it's a true deal-br=
197: eaker for the Bank, but we should not signal any flexibility at this stage.)
198: 
199: **(l) Representation re No Prior Control Agreements / Liens (Bank's =C2=A7 12=
200: )**
201: 
202: The Bank deleted the representation that there are no prior control agreement=
203: s or liens on the accounts.
204: 
205: **Reinstate.** This representation is critical to Pinnacle's perfection analy=
206: sis. The cover note should explain that we need this confirmation to ensure f=
207: irst-priority control.
208: 
209: **(m) Successor-Bank Notification Obligation (Bank's =C2=A7 13)**
210: 
211: The Bank deleted the obligation to notify the Secured Party before transferri=
212: ng accounts to a successor bank.
213: 
214: **Reinstate.** The successor notification is necessary to maintain the integr=
215: ity of the control arrangement. Propose that the Bank provide at least 30 day=
216: s' prior written notice of any merger, consolidation, or transfer of the acco=
217: unts.
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: **FEE PROVISIONS (Bank's =C2=A7 11)**
222: 
223: The Bank proposes an annual maintenance fee of $3,500 per account ($10,500 to=
224: tal for the three accounts) and a one-time legal-fee reimbursement of $15,000.
225: 
226: The annual fees are within market range and the client has indicated they're =
227: acceptable =E2=80=94 leave those as is. The one-time legal-fee reimbursement =
228: of $15,000 should be negotiated down. Propose a cap of $7,500 or actual docum=
229: ented fees, whichever is less. This is another area where we can demonstrate =
230: good faith without giving up anything material.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: **COORDINATION WITH DEBTOR'S COUNSEL**
235: 
236: Please coordinate with **Catherine Voss** at **Dunlevy Rourke LLP** (outside =
237: counsel to Graycliff) on any issues requiring Graycliff's consent or input =
238: =E2=80=94 in particular the account operation carve-out (item (b) above), the=
239:  set-off provisions (items (c) and (d)), and any indemnification obligations =
240: that flow to the Depositor. Graycliff's internal contact is Marcus Leung (SVP=
241:  & Treasurer).
242: 
243: Important: **do not share our internal strategy or fallback positions with Du=
244: nlevy Rourke.** Limit coordination to confirming Graycliff's consent to speci=
245: fic formulations.
246: 
247: ---
248: 
249: **LOGISTICS**
250: 
251: - Use our standard ACA negotiation playbook as a reference =E2=80=94 it shoul=
252: d cover most of the market-practice arguments you'll need.
253: - Both deliverables (redline and cover note) due to me by **EOD Friday, May 9=
254: **.
255: - The cover note should be addressed to Lena Marchetti and Reginald Stowe at =
256: Blackmere Fox LLP (301 South College Street, Suite 3200, Charlotte, NC 28202)=
257: , with copies to Catherine Voss at Dunlevy Rourke and Diana Whitford at Pinna=
258: cle. Check the forwarded email below =E2=80=94 if Jonathan Kehoe (Director =
259: =E2=80=93 Institutional Deposit Services, Ironbridge) was copied on the Bank =
260: counsel's transmittal, copy him on ours as well.
261: - Tone of the cover note should be professional and constructive. We want to =
262: keep this moving toward execution well ahead of May 30.
263: 
264: I'm available to discuss by phone Wednesday or Thursday if you want to walk t=
265: hrough any of the positions before you start drafting. Just grab time on my c=
266: alendar.
267: 
268: Thanks, Priya.
269: 
270: Tom

nt, by **May 30, 2025**. That's 46 calendar days from the Credit Agreement da=
te and roughly 24 days from today. We need to close out or substantially narr=
ow open issues in this turn =E2=80=94 we cannot afford extended back-and-fort=
h. UCC control over these deposit accounts must be perfected by that deadline=
to maintain valid security interests. Every round we add eats into that wind=
ow.
**CLIENT PRIORITIES**
I've spoken with Diana Whitford (VP =E2=80=93 Portfolio Management, Pinnacle)=
several times over the past week. Her priorities, in order:
1. **Strong, reliable control mechanics.** The ACA must give Pinnacle enforce=
able control over the deposit accounts once exclusive control is triggered. N=
o carve-outs or conditions that undercut that.
2. **Resist the Bank's liability cap.** The aggregate balances across the thr=
ee accounts are approximately **$38,150,000** (Operating ~$22.35M, Payroll ~$=
4.18M, Collections ~$11.62M). The Bank's proposed $50,000 cap is not remotely=
proportionate.
3. **New York governing law.**
**ISSUE-BY-ISSUE DIRECTION**
Address all 13 substantive changes in both the redline and the cover note. He=
re's my guidance:
**(a) Entitlement Order vs. Instruction Language (Bank's =C2=A7 2(a))**
The Bank substituted "instruction" for "entitlement order" throughout =C2=A7 =
2(a). Our form deliberately uses "entitlement order" language consistent with=
UCC Article 8.
**Non-negotiable.** Restore "entitlement order" throughout. The cover note sh=
ould explain this is necessary to ensure UCC Article 8 control and proper per=
fection. Don't leave room for ambiguity on this one.
**(b) Springing Exclusive Control / Account Operation Carve-Out (Bank's marku=
Our form provides for springing exclusive control upon default. The Bank's ma=
rkup adds a carve-out allowing Graycliff to continue operating the accounts w=
ithout Secured Party consent until delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control =
(NOEC).
**Non-negotiable on the springing structure itself.** We can accept =E2=80=94=
and our form already contemplates =E2=80=94 that Graycliff operates the acco=
unts in the ordinary course prior to NOEC delivery. But the Bank's carve-out =
language as drafted could undercut the effectiveness of exclusive control onc=
e an NOEC is delivered. Tighten the language so that (i) pre-NOEC ordinary co=
urse operation is clearly permitted, but (ii) upon delivery of an NOEC, Grayc=
liff's access is cut off without qualification. Make that distinction crisp.
**(c) Conflicting Instructions Waterfall / Bank Set-Off Priority (Bank's =C2=
The Bank's markup gives Bank set-off rights priority over Secured Party instr=
uctions in the conflicting-instructions waterfall.
**Resist.** Secured Party instructions must prevail. Cite the UCC control fra=
mework in the cover note =E2=80=94 the whole point of a control agreement is =
that the secured party's instructions override.
**(d) Set-Off Scope (Bank's =C2=A7 4)**
The Bank's markup permits set-off for "any obligation owed to Bank by Deposit=
or, whether direct or contingent."
**Some compromise is acceptable here.** We can live with a narrower set-off c=
arve-out limited to direct, matured, liquidated obligations arising under the=
deposit account agreements themselves =E2=80=94 but exclude contingent oblig=
ations, derivatives exposures, and affiliate obligations. Draft the narrower =
formulation and flag it in the cover note as a good-faith accommodation. This=
is an area where showing flexibility will serve us.
**(e) NOEC Compliance Period (Bank's =C2=A7 5)**
Our form says 2 business days; the Bank marked it up to 5.
**Counter at 3 business days.** That is the maximum the client will accept. F=
rame it as a reasonable middle ground in the cover note.
**(f) Indemnification / Gross Negligence (Bank's =C2=A7 6)**
The Bank's markup extends the indemnification obligation to cover the Bank's =
own gross negligence.
**Non-negotiable.** Reject this. Standard market practice does not require a =
secured party to indemnify a depository bank for the bank's own gross neglige=
nce. Restore the carve-out for gross negligence and willful misconduct. The c=
over note should be direct on this =E2=80=94 cite market practice.
**(g) Aggregate Liability Cap (Bank's =C2=A7 7(a))**
The Bank inserted a $50,000 aggregate liability cap.
**Non-negotiable in its current form.** As noted above, total controlled depo=
sits are approximately $38.15 million. A $50,000 cap is absurd and effectivel=
y eliminates any meaningful accountability. In the redline, delete the cap en=
tirely. As a fallback position (do not put this in the cover note =E2=80=94 t=
his is for our internal negotiation only), we could propose tying the cap to =
a percentage of or the actual aggregate balances in the controlled accounts. =
The cover note should make clear that $50,000 is unacceptable and explain why.
**(h) Consequential Damages Waiver (Bank's =C2=A7 7(b))**
The Bank inserted a mutual waiver of consequential, punitive, and indirect da=
mages.
Flag for discussion in the cover note but treat as lower priority given the o=
ther =C2=A7 7 issues. If we secure deletion or meaningful revision of the lia=
bility cap, a mutual consequential damages waiver becomes more palatable. Not=
e our reservation of rights to revisit but don't die on this hill in this tur=
n.
**(i) Set-Off Lookback / Subordination of Bank Lien (Bank's =C2=A7 8)**
Our form provides for full subordination of Bank liens. The Bank's markup lim=
its the subordination with a 90-day lookback cap.
**Resist at 90 days.** The client-directed minimum acceptable lookback is **1=
80 days**. Counter at 180 days and explain in the cover note that anything le=
ss creates a gap in the subordination protection that is unacceptable to the =
Secured Party.
**(j) Termination Rights (Bank's =C2=A7 9)**
Our form requires Secured Party consent for termination. The Bank's markup gi=
ves the Bank a unilateral right to terminate on 30 days' notice.
**Resist unilateral termination.** As a fallback, propose a minimum of **90 d=
ays' written notice** with an express right for the Secured Party to transiti=
on the accounts to a replacement depository bank during the notice period. Th=
e cover note should emphasize that abrupt termination could impair perfection=
of the security interest.
**(k) Governing Law (Bank's change)**
Our form specifies New York. The Bank changed to North Carolina.
**Push for New York in this turn.** Present it as firm in the cover note. (Be=
tween us =E2=80=94 this may ultimately be a concession if it's a true deal-br=
eaker for the Bank, but we should not signal any flexibility at this stage.)
**(l) Representation re No Prior Control Agreements / Liens (Bank's =C2=A7 12=
The Bank deleted the representation that there are no prior control agreement=
s or liens on the accounts.
**Reinstate.** This representation is critical to Pinnacle's perfection analy=
sis. The cover note should explain that we need this confirmation to ensure f=
irst-priority control.
**(m) Successor-Bank Notification Obligation (Bank's =C2=A7 13)**
The Bank deleted the obligation to notify the Secured Party before transferri=
ng accounts to a successor bank.
**Reinstate.** The successor notification is necessary to maintain the integr=
ity of the control arrangement. Propose that the Bank provide at least 30 day=
s' prior written notice of any merger, consolidation, or transfer of the acco=
unts.
**FEE PROVISIONS (Bank's =C2=A7 11)**
The Bank proposes an annual maintenance fee of $3,500 per account ($10,500 to=
tal for the three accounts) and a one-time legal-fee reimbursement of $15,000.
The annual fees are within market range and the client has indicated they're =
acceptable =E2=80=94 leave those as is. The one-time legal-fee reimbursement =
of $15,000 should be negotiated down. Propose a cap of $7,500 or actual docum=
ented fees, whichever is less. This is another area where we can demonstrate =
good faith without giving up anything material.
**COORDINATION WITH DEBTOR'S COUNSEL**
Please coordinate with **Catherine Voss** at **Dunlevy Rourke LLP** (outside =
counsel to Graycliff) on any issues requiring Graycliff's consent or input =

set-off provisions (items (c) and (d)), and any indemnification obligations =

nlevy Rourke.** Limit coordination to confirming Graycliff's consent to speci=

**LOGISTICS**

d cover most of the market-practice arguments you'll need.
- Both deliverables (redline and cover note) due to me by **EOD Friday, May 9=
- The cover note should be addressed to Lena Marchetti and Reginald Stowe at =
Blackmere Fox LLP (301 South College Street, Suite 3200, Charlotte, NC 28202)=
, with copies to Catherine Voss at Dunlevy Rourke and Diana Whitford at Pinna=
cle. Check the forwarded email below =E2=80=94 if Jonathan Kehoe (Director =
=E2=80=93 Institutional Deposit Services, Ironbridge) was copied on the Bank =
counsel's transmittal, copy him on ours as well.

keep this moving toward execution well ahead of May 30.
I'm available to discuss by phone Wednesday or Thursday if you want to walk t=

alendar.
Thanks, Priya.
Tom

Hargrave Stein & Collier LLP

1: **[PINNACLE CAPITAL PARTNERS, LLC]{.underline}**
2: 
3: **[ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT --- NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK]{.underline}**
4: 
5: **Prepared by Hargrave Stein & Collier LLP**
6: 
7: **787 Seventh Avenue, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019**
8: 
9: **Hargrave Stein Matter No.: 2025-HSC-04417**
10: 
11: **PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT**
12: 
13: *This playbook is prepared for the exclusive use of Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC and its internal personnel in connection with the negotiation of deposit account control agreements across Pinnacle\'s secured lending portfolio. It is not intended for distribution to counterparties, depository banks, or borrower\'s counsel. This document reflects legal strategy and attorney mental impressions and is protected by the attorney-client privilege and work product doctrine.*
14: 
15: *Last Updated: April 2025*
16: 
17: *Lead Contact: Thomas Orr, Partner --- torr@hargravestein.com* *Associate Contact: Priya Nagarajan --- pnagarajan@hargravestein.com*
18: 
19: **[SECTION 1 --- INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE]{.underline}**
20: 
21: **[1.1 --- Purpose of This Playbook]{.underline}**
22: 
23: This playbook serves as a standing reference for Hargrave Stein & Collier LLP attorneys and Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC (\"Pinnacle\") internal personnel --- including Diana Whitford, Vice President -- Portfolio Management, and her team --- when negotiating deposit account control agreements (\"ACAs\" or \"DACAs\") with depository banks in connection with Pinnacle\'s revolving credit facilities and other secured lending transactions. The document is designed to be used as a real-time negotiation tool, enabling the assigned negotiator to respond promptly and consistently to bank markup positions without the delay inherent in seeking ad hoc client instructions on each individual issue.
24: 
25: The playbook is organized by issue category corresponding to common bank markup positions and covers the universe of substantive provisions typically found in tripartite ACAs among the secured party, the depositor (borrower or guarantor), and the depository bank. The issue categories addressed herein reflect the full range of provisions that have been the subject of negotiation in Pinnacle\'s ACA transactions over the past three years, including the firm\'s ongoing engagement with Ironbridge National Bank, N.A. in the Graycliff Industries, Inc. transaction (Matter No. 2025-HSC-04417).
26: 
27: For each issue category, the playbook sets forth three tiers of negotiating positions:
28: 
29: > **(a)** **Green --- Pinnacle\'s Preferred/Ideal Position.** This tier reflects the language contained in Pinnacle\'s form ACA, which represents Pinnacle\'s optimal position on each issue. The form ACA has been drafted to maximize Pinnacle\'s protections and to satisfy all requirements for \"control\" under UCC § 9-104. The preferred position should be the starting point in every negotiation and should be defended through at least the first round of counter-markups.
30: >
31: > **(b)** **Yellow --- Acceptable Fallback Positions.** This tier sets forth one or more compromise positions, with sample counter-language, that may be offered to the depository bank without further client approval from the deal team. These fallback positions have been pre-authorized by Diana Whitford and reflect the maximum concession that the deal team has determined is consistent with Pinnacle\'s risk parameters. Where multiple fallback positions are available within a single issue category, they are presented in order of preference (Fallback A is preferred over Fallback B, which is preferred over Fallback C), and the negotiator should exhaust each fallback before moving to the next.
32: >
33: > **(c)** **Red --- Walk-Away / Escalation Triggers.** This tier identifies positions that require express approval from the deal team (Diana Whitford or her designee) before any concession is offered. In certain cases, a bank position is identified as a \"hard stop\" --- meaning it cannot be accepted under any circumstances because it would destroy Pinnacle\'s control over the deposit accounts for UCC perfection purposes or otherwise create unacceptable legal risk. Hard-stop positions should be communicated clearly and firmly to bank counsel, with an explanation of the structural basis for the objection.
34: 
35: This playbook reflects Pinnacle\'s current risk posture as of April 2025 and should be revisited semi-annually or upon material changes in market practice, UCC amendments, or judicial decisions affecting deposit account control. The next scheduled review is October 2025. Any interim developments --- including significant judicial decisions, regulatory guidance, or changes in Pinnacle\'s collateral policy --- should be communicated promptly to Thomas Orr or Priya Nagarajan for incorporation into the playbook.
36: 
37: **[1.2 --- Legal Framework: UCC Perfection over Deposit Accounts]{.underline}**
38: 
39: An understanding of the Uniform Commercial Code\'s requirements for perfection of a security interest in deposit accounts is essential to the effective negotiation of every ACA provision. This section provides a summary of the applicable legal framework, which should inform the negotiator\'s analysis of every bank markup.
40: 
41: **Perfection by Control Only.** Under UCC Article 9, \"control\" is the sole method of perfection of a security interest in a deposit account as original collateral. UCC § 9-312(b)(1) expressly provides that a security interest in a deposit account may be perfected only by control under UCC § 9-104. Filing a UCC-1 financing statement is insufficient to perfect a security interest in a deposit account as original collateral; although a financing statement may be filed to provide notice to third parties, it does not constitute perfection and does not establish priority. This distinguishes deposit accounts from most other categories of personal property collateral, where filing is the primary method of perfection. The consequence is that the ACA is not merely a supplemental perfection device --- it is the *only* mechanism by which Pinnacle can obtain a perfected security interest in its borrowers\' deposit account balances.
42: 
43: **Methods of Obtaining Control.** A secured party obtains \"control\" of a deposit account under UCC § 9-104 by one of three methods:
44: 
45: > **(i)** *Customer Method (§ 9-104(a)(1)):* The secured party becomes the bank\'s customer on the account --- i.e., the account is maintained in the secured party\'s name or the secured party is added as an account holder. This method is rarely used in commercial lending transactions because it requires the borrower to surrender account ownership.
46: >
47: > **(ii)** *Tripartite Agreement Method (§ 9-104(a)(2)):* The bank has agreed, in an authenticated record, to comply with instructions originated by the secured party directing the disposition of funds in the deposit account without further consent of the depositor. This is the method addressed by the standard ACA and is the method on which Pinnacle relies in substantially all of its secured lending transactions.
48: >
49: > **(iii)** *Bank-as-Secured-Party Method (§ 9-104(a)(3)):* The secured party is the depository bank itself. This method is available only to the bank at which the deposit account is maintained and is not relevant to Pinnacle\'s position as an external secured party.
50: 
51: **Pinnacle\'s ACA --- Tripartite Agreement Method.** Pinnacle\'s standard form ACA is designed to satisfy method (ii) --- the tripartite agreement among Pinnacle (as secured party), the borrower or guarantor (as depositor), and the depository bank. Under this method, the bank must agree in an authenticated record to comply with instructions originated by Pinnacle directing the disposition of the funds in the controlled accounts, and it must agree to do so *without further consent of the depositor*. This last requirement --- the absence of a depositor consent condition --- is the sine qua non of control under UCC § 9-104(a)(2). Every provision of the ACA must be evaluated through the lens of whether it preserves or undermines Pinnacle\'s \"control\" for purposes of this statutory requirement.
52: 
53: **Critical Caution --- Depositor Consent Conditions.** Any bank markup that conditions the bank\'s obligation to comply with Pinnacle\'s instructions on depositor consent, depositor notice, or any approval right of the depositor after delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control (\"NOEC\") risks destroying the very control that the ACA is designed to establish and thus imperils perfection. The statutory language of UCC § 9-104(a)(2) is clear: the bank must agree to comply with the secured party\'s instructions \"without further consent of the debtor.\" A provision that reintroduces a depositor consent requirement --- whether framed as a \"consent,\" \"confirmation,\" \"acknowledgment,\" \"non-objection,\" or any equivalent formulation --- is fundamentally inconsistent with the statute and must be rejected. This principle is the single most important guideline in this playbook and applies across all issue categories.
54: 
55: **Cross-Reference to Article 8.** For the related but distinct question of whether the controlled account should be characterized as a \"securities account\" or \"deposit account\" --- and the implications of that characterization for the applicable control analysis --- see Section 2 of this playbook, which addresses UCC Article 8 vs. Article 9 control language.
56: 
57: **[1.3 --- Typical Transaction Context]{.underline}**
58: 
59: Pinnacle\'s ACAs most commonly arise in connection with revolving credit facilities where the applicable Credit Agreement requires delivery of ACAs over the borrower\'s principal deposit accounts within a specified post-closing period. The typical Credit Agreement provision is found in the post-closing obligations section (e.g., Credit Agreement § 6.14(b), or the equivalent provision in Pinnacle\'s form credit agreement), which requires delivery of fully executed ACAs within 30 to 60 calendar days of the closing date. In some transactions, the ACA delivery obligation is a condition to initial or subsequent advances; in others, it is a standalone covenant the breach of which constitutes an Event of Default if not cured within the applicable cure period.
60: 
61: Negotiators must track the applicable perfection deadline for each transaction and manage the bank negotiation timeline accordingly. Delays in ACA execution leave Pinnacle with an unperfected security interest in deposit account balances, creating a gap in the collateral package that exposes Pinnacle to the risk that a competing creditor --- including a bankruptcy trustee --- could obtain priority over the deposit account balances. In a bankruptcy scenario, an unperfected security interest in a deposit account is avoidable by the trustee under Section 544(a) of the Bankruptcy Code (the \"strong arm\" clause), with the result that the deposit account balances would be treated as unencumbered property of the estate. The urgency of timely ACA execution cannot be overstated.
62: 
63: In Pinnacle\'s current active matters, controlled deposit balances range from approximately \$10 million to \$50 million per borrower across multiple accounts. ACA negotiation effort should be proportionate to the value of the collateral at stake. For transactions involving controlled deposit balances in excess of \$25 million, the full negotiation playbook should be applied with rigor; for smaller balances, the negotiator retains discretion to prioritize critical structural issues (Sections 2 through 5) and accept reasonable bank positions on secondary issues (Sections 6 through 13) to expedite execution.
64: 
65: **[1.4 --- How to Use This Playbook]{.underline}**
66: 
67: The playbook is organized around the three-tier framework described in Section 1.1 above: **Green** (preferred position), **Yellow** (acceptable fallback --- pre-authorized for concession without further client approval), and **Red** (escalation required before any concession is offered). This framework applies to each issue category covered in Sections 2 through 14.
68: 
69: When a bank returns a markup of the ACA, the negotiator should follow the process set forth below:
70: 
71: > **Step 1 --- Issue Mapping.** Map each substantive bank change to the corresponding playbook section. If a bank change does not correspond to a specific playbook section, flag it for review by Thomas Orr or Priya Nagarajan.
72: >
73: > **Step 2 --- Tier Classification.** For each bank change, determine whether the bank\'s position falls within the Green, Yellow, or Red tier for the applicable issue category.
74: >
75: > **Step 3 --- Counter-Markup Preparation.** Prepare a redline response that (a) rejects all Red-tier bank positions and restores Pinnacle\'s preferred language (unless escalation has resulted in client authorization to concede), (b) addresses Yellow-tier issues by first attempting to achieve the Green position and offering fallback language only if the bank has rejected or pushed back on the preferred position, and (c) accepts any bank changes that are consistent with Pinnacle\'s preferred position or are immaterial.
76: 
77: A critical reminder: even where a fallback position is pre-authorized under this playbook, the negotiator should attempt to achieve the preferred (Green) position in the first counter-markup. Fallback language should be offered only after the bank has rejected or pushed back on the preferred position in a prior round of negotiation. Opening with a fallback position signals unnecessary flexibility and may invite further bank pushback on other issues.
78: 
79: The playbook is designed to be used in conjunction with Pinnacle\'s form ACA, which should be delivered to the depository bank as the initial draft in every transaction where Pinnacle controls the documentation process. Where the bank insists on using its own form ACA, the negotiator should map the bank\'s form against Pinnacle\'s form, identify all deviations, and treat each deviation as a bank markup subject to the playbook\'s three-tier analysis.
