Bank’s compliance obligation is unconditional and is not subject to any condition precedent other than delivery in accordance with the notice and authentication provisions of this Agreement.','Restores dual-track control language without requiring Depositor consent.')
add_body(red,'2.3 No Changes to Accounts Without Consent. Bank shall not, without the prior written consent of Secured Party, change the name, account number, title, designation or ownership of an Account; close, terminate or redesignate an Account; open an Account intended to be subject to this Agreement; merge or combine an Account; or permit a change to authorized signatories objected to in writing by Secured Party.')
add_body(red,'2.4 Depositor’s Consent. Depositor irrevocably authorizes and consents to Bank’s compliance with all Instructions and Entitlement Orders originated by Secured Party, without inquiry into Secured Party’s authority and without notice to Depositor. Depositor acknowledges that Bank shall have no liability to Depositor for complying in accordance with this Agreement.')
add_revision_paragraph(red,'2.5 Depositor’s Operating Rights Prior to Notice of Exclusive Control.','Unless and until Bank has received a Notice of Exclusive Control, Depositor shall have the full and unrestricted right to issue Instructions with respect to the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, without consent or notification to Secured Party.','Prior to Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Depositor may operate the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, including withdrawals, transfers, payments, ACH transactions and other customary banking transactions, without prior consent of Secured Party. This ordinary-course permission terminates immediately upon Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control; after that receipt, Bank shall not accept or process any new Depositor Instruction, and Depositor shall have no right to withdraw funds or give Instructions with respect to the Accounts.','Preserves the Bank’s operational concern only before NOEC; no post-NOEC carve-out.')

Bank shall comply immediately with Secured Party’s Instructions and shall not give priority to any inconsistent Depositor Instruction. After receipt of a NOEC, Bank shall comply exclusively with Secured Party’s Instructions and shall not be required to follow any Depositor Instruction.','Rejects Bank priority; Secured Party control is the agreed waterfall.')
add_revision_paragraph(red,'4.2 Notice of Conflicts.','Bank shall have no liability to Secured Party for complying with Bank’s own rights in priority to Secured Party’s Instructions.','Bank shall promptly, and in any event within one (1) Business Day, notify Secured Party in writing of any conflicting or potentially conflicting Depositor Instruction and shall await further direction from Secured Party before acting on that Instruction, except to the extent delay would violate applicable law.','Provides visibility without granting Bank discretion to override Secured Party.')

def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)


def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:

            node = OxmlElement(f'w:{m}')
            tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v))
        node.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa')


def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)


def add_field(paragraph, field):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = field
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)
    return run


def set_run_props(r, bold=False, italic=False, underline=False, color=None, strike=False, size=None, font='Arial'):
    rPr = r.get_or_add_rPr()
    rFonts = rPr.rPr.rFonts if hasattr(rPr.rPr, 'rFonts') else None
    # python-docx run rPr wrapper is easier via children
    rf = rPr.find(qn('w:rFonts'))
    if rf is None:
        rf = OxmlElement('w:rFonts'); rPr.append(rf)
    rf.set(qn('w:ascii'), font); rf.set(qn('w:hAnsi'), font); rf.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), font)
    if bold:
        b = OxmlElement('w:b'); rPr.append(b)
    if italic:
        i = OxmlElement('w:i'); rPr.append(i)
    if underline:
        u = OxmlElement('w:u'); u.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); rPr.append(u)
    if strike:
        s = OxmlElement('w:strike'); rPr.append(s)
    if color:
        c = OxmlElement('w:color'); c.set(qn('w:val'), color); rPr.append(c)
    if size:
        sz = OxmlElement('w:sz'); sz.set(qn('w:val'), str(int(size*2))); rPr.append(sz)
        szcs = OxmlElement('w:szCs'); szcs.set(qn('w:val'), str(int(size*2))); rPr.append(szcs)


def add_normal(p, text, bold=False, italic=False, underline=False, color=None, strike=False, size=None):
    r = p.add_run(text)
    if any([bold, italic, underline, color, strike, size]):
        set_run_props(r._r, bold, italic, underline, color, strike, size)
    return r


def add_tracked(p, text, kind='ins', author='Pinnacle / Hargrave Stein', date='2025-05-09T12:00:00Z'):
    wrapper = OxmlElement('w:ins' if kind == 'ins' else 'w:del')
    wrapper.set(qn('w:id'), '1' if kind == 'ins' else '2')
    wrapper.set(qn('w:author'), author)
    wrapper.set(qn('w:date'), date)
    r = OxmlElement('w:r')
    rPr = OxmlElement('w:rPr')
    rf = OxmlElement('w:rFonts'); rf.set(qn('w:ascii'), 'Arial'); rf.set(qn('w:hAnsi'), 'Arial'); rPr.append(rf)
    if kind == 'ins':
        u = OxmlElement('w:u'); u.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); rPr.append(u)
        c = OxmlElement('w:color'); c.set(qn('w:val'), BLUE); rPr.append(c)
    else:
        s = OxmlElement('w:strike'); rPr.append(s)
        c = OxmlElement('w:color'); c.set(qn('w:val'), RED); rPr.append(c)
    r.append(rPr)
    t = OxmlElement('w:t' if kind == 'ins' else 'w:delText')
    if text.startswith(' ') or text.endswith(' ') or '  ' in text:
        t.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve')
    t.text = text
    r.append(t); wrapper.append(r); p._p.append(wrapper)
    return wrapper


def add_revision_paragraph(doc, label, old, new, note=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    add_normal(p, label + ' ', bold=True)
    add_tracked(p, old, 'del')
    add_tracked(p, new, 'ins')
    if note:
        add_normal(p, '  [' + note + ']', italic=True, color=GRAY, size=9)
    return p


def add_heading(doc, text, level=1):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(12 if level==1 else 8)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
    add_normal(p, text, bold=True, color=BLUE, size=14 if level==1 else 11)
    return p


def add_body(doc, text, bold_prefix=None, italic=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        add_normal(p, bold_prefix, bold=True)
        add_normal(p, text[len(bold_prefix):], italic=italic)
    else:
        add_normal(p, text, italic=italic)
    return p


def add_bullet(doc, text, level=0):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet' if level==0 else 'List Bullet 2')
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    add_normal(p, text)
    return p


def setup_doc(doc, title):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(0.7); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.65); sec.left_margin = Inches(0.75); sec.right_margin = Inches(0.75)

    styles['Normal'].font.name = 'Arial'; styles['Normal'].font.size = Pt(9.5)
    styles['Normal']._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Arial')
    for name in ['List Bullet','List Bullet 2']:
        styles[name].font.name='Arial'; styles[name].font.size=Pt(9.5)
    styles['List Bullet']._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'),'Arial')
    header = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    header.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    add_normal(header, 'CONFIDENTIAL — DRAFT FOR DISCUSSION', bold=True, color=GRAY, size=8)

    add_normal(footer, 'Hargrave Stein & Collier LLP | Matter No. 2025-HSC-04417 | May 9, 2025  •  Page ', color=GRAY, size=8)
    add_field(footer, 'PAGE')
    settings = doc.settings.element
    for tag in ['w:trackRevisions','w:doNotTrackMoves']:
        el = OxmlElement(tag); settings.append(el)
    doc.core_properties.title = title
    doc.core_properties.author = 'Hargrave Stein & Collier LLP'

The distinction after an NOEC is critical, however: upon Ironbridge’s receipt of an NOEC, the pre-NOEC operating permission terminates immediately, Ironbridge must not accept or process new Depositor Instructions, and exclusive compliance with Pinnacle’s Instructions begins. This structure is central to the UCC control framework and is necessary to ensure that the account-control arrangement works when the Secured Party needs to exercise its remedies.'),

The carve-out excludes contingent, disputed, unliquidated or unmatured obligations, derivatives, swaps, foreign exchange, letters of credit, unrelated credit facilities and affiliate obligations. body(red,'The following provisions set out the operative Turn 2 language for the affected provisions. The Bank’s agreed factual information has been carried forward: the Accounts are the Operating Account ending -4471, Payroll Account ending -4472, and Collections Account ending -4473, all maintained at Ironbridge National Bank, N.A.; the approximate aggregate balance is $38,150,000; and the Credit Agreement is dated April 14, 2025, with a May 30, 2025 delivery deadline under §6.14(b).')
heading(red,'Parties and Recitals — Agreed Bank Turn 1 Facts',2)
body(red,'This DEPOSIT ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of [DATE], 2025 (the “Effective Date”), by and among Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as secured party (the “Secured Party”); Graycliff Industries, Inc., a Delaware corporation, as depositor/debtor (the “Depositor”); and Ironbridge National Bank, N.A., a national banking association (the “Bank”).')
body(red,'Depositor maintains the Accounts identified on Schedule A. Secured Party has been granted a security interest in the Accounts and the funds therein under the Credit Agreement dated April 14, 2025, maturing April 14, 2030, and the related Loan Documents. The Parties enter into this Agreement to establish control over the Accounts for purposes of perfection under the UCC.')
heading(red,'Section 1 — Definitions',1)
body(red,'“Account” means each deposit account identified on Schedule A, including renewals, replacements, reclassifications, redesignations and successor accounts, and all funds and proceeds credited thereto.')
body(red,'“Business Day” means a day on which Bank is open for substantially all commercial banking business at its offices in Charlotte, North Carolina, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and days on which banking institutions in North Carolina are authorized or required to close.')
revision(red,'“Entitlement Order.”','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the definition of “Entitlement Order” and used “Instructions” only in the operative control provisions.]','“Entitlement Order” has the meaning assigned to that term in UCC §8-102(a)(8) and includes any notification communicated to Bank directing the transfer, redemption, liquidation or other disposition of a financial asset or interest therein, including any instruction originated by Secured Party pursuant to this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, the use of “Entitlement Order” does not, by itself, characterize any Account as a securities account or Bank as a securities intermediary.','Restores Article 8 term on a conditional, belt-and-suspenders basis.')
body(red,'“Event of Default,” “Notice of Exclusive Control” or “NOEC,” “Instructions,” “Lien,” “Loan Documents,” and “UCC” have the meanings assigned in the Bank Turn 1 document, except that references to the UCC shall be read consistently with the New York governing-law and applicable-jurisdiction provisions below.')
heading(red,'Section 2 — The Accounts; Establishment of Control',1)
body(red,'2.1 Confirmation of Accounts. Bank confirms that each Account listed on Schedule A is maintained at Bank, is held in the name of Depositor, and constitutes a “deposit account” within the meaning of the UCC. Bank is the “bank” within the meaning of UCC §9-102(a)(8) with respect to each Account.')
revision(red,'2.2 Establishment of Control.','Bank hereby agrees that, from and after the Effective Date, it will comply with Instructions originated by Secured Party directing the disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent of Depositor, thereby establishing control under UCC §9-104(a)(2).','Bank hereby agrees that, from and after the Effective Date, it will comply with Entitlement Orders and Instructions originated by Secured Party directing the disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent of Depositor, thereby establishing control by Secured Party over the Accounts within the meaning of UCC §§9-104(a)(2) and 8-106, to the extent applicable. Bank’s compliance obligation is unconditional and is not subject to any condition precedent other than delivery in accordance with the notice and authentication provisions of this Agreement.','Restores dual-track control language without requiring Depositor consent.')
body(red,'2.3 No Changes to Accounts Without Consent. Bank shall not, without the prior written consent of Secured Party, change the name, account number, title, designation or ownership of an Account; close, terminate or redesignate an Account; open an Account intended to be subject to this Agreement; merge or combine an Account; or permit a change to authorized signatories objected to in writing by Secured Party.')
body(red,'2.4 Depositor’s Consent. Depositor irrevocably authorizes and consents to Bank’s compliance with all Instructions and Entitlement Orders originated by Secured Party, without inquiry into Secured Party’s authority and without notice to Depositor. Depositor acknowledges that Bank shall have no liability to Depositor for complying in accordance with this Agreement.')
revision(red,'2.5 Depositor’s Operating Rights Prior to Notice of Exclusive Control.','Unless and until Bank has received a Notice of Exclusive Control, Depositor shall have the full and unrestricted right to issue Instructions with respect to the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, without consent or notification to Secured Party.','Prior to Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Depositor may operate the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, including withdrawals, transfers, payments, ACH transactions and other customary banking transactions, without prior consent of Secured Party. This ordinary-course permission terminates immediately upon Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control; after that receipt, Bank shall not accept or process any new Depositor Instruction, and Depositor shall have no right to withdraw funds or give Instructions with respect to the Accounts.','Preserves the Bank’s operational concern only before NOEC; no post-NOEC carve-out.')
heading(red,'Section 3 — Exclusive Control Upon Notice of Exclusive Control',1)
revision(red,'3.1 Effect of Notice of Exclusive Control.','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the former Section 3 and replaced it with Bank Priority / Set-Off Rights.]','Upon Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control delivered in accordance with Section 10: (a) Bank shall immediately cease complying with all Instructions originated by or on behalf of Depositor and shall reject, refuse to honor and return unpaid any Depositor payment order presented or received after such receipt; (b) Bank shall comply solely and exclusively with Instructions and Entitlement Orders originated by or on behalf of Secured Party, including transfers, withdrawals, account closing and delivery of statements; (c) Bank shall freeze and block all automated or preauthorized debits and recurring transactions originated by Depositor; and (d) Bank shall provide Secured Party with current balance and transaction information promptly upon request. Bank shall not require Depositor consent, approval, confirmation or other authorization as a condition to compliance.','Restores springing exclusive control and makes the post-NOEC cutoff unconditional.')
body(red,'3.2 No Requirement of Proof. Bank shall not require evidence of an Event of Default, a court order, judgment, Depositor certificate or other documentation as a condition to compliance with a NOEC. Bank’s sole obligation is to verify that the NOEC is written, purports to come from Secured Party or its authorized representative, is delivered in accordance with Section 10, and directs exclusive compliance with Secured Party’s Instructions.')
body(red,'3.3 Rescission. A NOEC remains in effect until Secured Party delivers a written rescission notice. Upon receipt of a rescission notice, Section 2.5 shall again apply. Bank shall comply with a rescission notice within two (2) Business Days.')
heading(red,'Section 4 — Conflicting Instructions; Waterfall',1)
revision(red,'4.1 Priority of Instructions.','Bank’s rights of set-off, recoupment, banker’s lien and security interest shall at all times be prior and superior to Instructions received from Secured Party.','In the event of a conflict between Instructions or Entitlement Orders received from Secured Party and Instructions received from Depositor, the Instructions and Entitlement Orders of Secured Party shall control and prevail at all times, whether or not a NOEC has been delivered. Bank shall comply immediately with Secured Party’s Instructions and shall not give priority to any inconsistent Depositor Instruction. After receipt of a NOEC, Bank shall comply exclusively with Secured Party’s Instructions and shall not be required to follow any Depositor Instruction.','Rejects Bank priority; Secured Party control is the agreed waterfall.')
revision(red,'4.2 Notice of Conflicts.','Bank shall have no liability to Secured Party for complying with Bank’s own rights in priority to Secured Party’s Instructions.','Bank shall promptly, and in any event within one (1) Business Day, notify Secured Party in writing of any conflicting or potentially conflicting Depositor Instruction and shall await further direction from Secured Party before acting on that Instruction, except to the extent delay would violate applicable law.','Provides visibility without granting Bank discretion to override Secured Party.')
heading(red,'Section 5 — Set-Off Scope and NOEC Compliance Period',1)
revision(red,'5.1 Permitted Set-Off Scope.','Bank reserves and retains the unrestricted right to set off, charge, debit or apply funds against any obligation owed to Bank by Depositor, whether direct or contingent, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, and whether or not related to the Accounts.','Subject to Sections 4 and 8, Bank may exercise set-off only with respect to obligations of Depositor to Bank that are (a) direct, (b) matured, liquidated and then due and payable, and (c) arising directly under deposit account agreements between Bank and Depositor relating to the Accounts. Bank shall not exercise set-off for any contingent, disputed, unliquidated or unmatured obligation, any obligation arising under a derivative, swap, foreign exchange, letter-of-credit, credit facility or other unrelated agreement, or any obligation owed to an affiliate of Bank.','Good-faith accommodation; excludes contingent and unrelated exposures.')
body(red,'5.2 No Prior Notice or Consent Required. Bank may exercise a permitted set-off without prior notice to or consent of Secured Party, subject to the scope and priority limitations in this Agreement and the Bank’s obligation to notify Secured Party promptly after exercise.')
revision(red,'5.3 NOEC Compliance Period.','Bank shall comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control within five (5) Business Days of receipt thereof.','Bank shall comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control beginning no later than the third (3rd) Business Day following Bank’s receipt and authentication of the Notice of Exclusive Control. During that period, Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement the NOEC as promptly as practicable and shall not permit new debits, withdrawals or transfers initiated by Depositor after Bank’s receipt of the NOEC.','Three Business Days is the maximum client-approved period.')
heading(red,'Section 6 — Indemnification',1)
revision(red,'6.1–6.2 Secured Party Indemnification.','The indemnification obligations of Secured Party shall apply regardless of whether Losses arise in whole or in part from the negligence (including gross negligence) of Bank, and shall be limited only where Losses are determined to have resulted solely and directly from Bank’s willful misconduct.','The Depositor and Secured Party, jointly and severally, shall indemnify and hold harmless Bank and its officers, directors, employees and agents from claims, losses, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising out of Bank’s performance of its obligations or compliance with Secured Party’s Instructions; provided, however, that the indemnification shall not extend to claims, losses, liabilities, costs or expenses to the extent arising from Bank’s own gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith.','Restores the market-standard gross-negligence, willful-misconduct and bad-faith carve-out.')
body(red,'6.3 Depositor Indemnification. Depositor’s indemnity for its breach, inaccurate representations and third-party claims remains as set out in Bank Turn 1, subject to the foregoing carve-out for Bank conduct.')
heading(red,'Section 7 — Limitation of Liability',1)
revision(red,'7.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.','Bank’s aggregate liability under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000). The limitation shall not apply only to Losses resulting from Bank’s willful misconduct.','[DELETED IN FULL — NO AGGREGATE LIABILITY CAP.]','The proposed cap is deleted; the controlled deposits total approximately $38.15 million.')
revision(red,'7.2 Consequential Damages.','NO PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO ANY OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES OF ANY KIND WHATSOEVER, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT, NEGLIGENCE, STRICT LIABILITY OR ANY OTHER THEORY, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY.','No party shall be liable to any other party for any indirect, consequential, special, punitive or exemplary damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement, regardless of the form of action or theory of liability; provided that this Section shall not limit the obligations of Depositor or Secured Party under Section 6 or limit recovery of direct damages, including amounts released from an Account in breach of this Agreement.','Mutual waiver accepted on a clarified basis; direct account-balance damages and indemnity remain available.')
body(red,'7.3 No Duty to Monitor; 7.4 Good Faith Reliance; 7.5 No Fiduciary Duty. These Bank Turn 1 provisions remain unchanged, except that good-faith reliance does not excuse a breach caused by Bank’s gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith.')
heading(red,'Section 8 — Subordination of Bank Liens; Waiver of Set-Off',1)
revision(red,'8.1 Limited Subordination / Lookback Period.','Bank agrees to subordinate its Liens solely to the extent of fees, charges and returned items accrued or incurred during the ninety (90) day period immediately preceding delivery of a NOEC, and Liens arising before that period or after delivery of the NOEC remain prior and superior.','Bank shall subordinate its Liens, security interests, claims, counterclaims and rights of set-off in the Accounts and funds therein to the security interest of Secured Party; provided that, as a negotiated accommodation, Bank may retain the limited rights described in Section 5.1 only for obligations arising during the one hundred eighty (180) day period immediately preceding delivery of a NOEC. No Bank Lien or set-off right for a period shorter than one hundred eighty (180) days, or for a post-NOEC obligation other than customary documented account fees and return items, shall be prior to Secured Party’s security interest.','Counters the 90-day period at the client-directed 180-day minimum.')
body(red,'8.2 Fee and Return-Item Exceptions. Bank may debit customary, documented maintenance fees, service charges and return items directly attributable to the Accounts in accordance with the agreed fee schedule, but such charges shall not be used to defeat Secured Party’s control or priority.')
heading(red,'Section 9 — Successor Bank; Termination',1)
revision(red,'Section 9 heading and successor provisions.','Section 9 — [DELETED: Successor Bank; Notification Obligations] [ADDED: Termination]','Section 9 — Successor Bank; Notification Obligations; Termination','Restores successor-bank continuity and keeps the Bank’s termination request subject to transition protections.')
revision(red,'9.1 Successor Bank Notification.','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the successor-bank notification obligation in its entirety.]','Bank shall provide Secured Party at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice of any proposed merger, consolidation, assignment, transfer of the Accounts, change of charter or other succession event that would result in a successor bank holding the Accounts. Any successor bank shall be bound by this Agreement, and Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a written assumption of Bank’s obligations; provided that the notice obligation applies to the extent legally permissible.','Thirty days’ prior written notice is required to maintain visibility and continuity.')
body(red,'9.2 Termination by Secured Party; 9.3 No Unilateral Termination by Depositor. The Bank Turn 1 provisions remain unchanged.')
revision(red,'9.4 Bank Termination.','Bank may terminate this Agreement, in its sole discretion, upon thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, without any requirement that a successor bank be appointed or a replacement agreement executed.','Bank may terminate this Agreement only upon not less than ninety (90) days’ prior written notice to Secured Party and Depositor; provided that (i) during the notice period Bank shall continue to comply with all obligations hereunder, including any outstanding NOEC, (ii) Depositor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts at a depository bank reasonably acceptable to Secured Party and deliver a replacement ACA reasonably satisfactory to Secured Party, and (iii) this Agreement shall not terminate until Secured Party confirms in writing that the replacement ACA has been executed and delivered. Bank shall cooperate with the transition and provide account statements and transaction information reasonably requested by Secured Party.','Fallback transition language; prevents a perfection gap.')
heading(red,'Section 10 — Notices; Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Miscellaneous',1)
body(red,'10.1 Notices. The Bank Turn 1 notice methods, notice addresses and authentication procedures remain unchanged, with the Account contacts and addresses shown in the Bank Turn 1 document.')
revision(red,'10.2 Governing Law.','This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles.','This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and interpreted in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles thereof that would require or permit application of the laws of another jurisdiction. Matters relating to perfection, priority and enforcement of security interests in the Accounts shall be determined under the UCC as in effect in the applicable jurisdiction under UCC §9-304.','Restores consistency with the Credit Agreement and Loan Documents.')
revision(red,'10.3 Jurisdiction; Venue.','Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina.','Each Party irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York and the Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York, and the appellate courts thereof, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement.','Restores the New York forum selected in Pinnacle’s form.')
body(red,'10.4 Waiver of Jury Trial; 10.5 Amendments; 10.6 Entire Agreement; 10.7 Severability; 10.8 Counterparts and Electronic Execution; 10.9 Successors and Assigns; 10.10 No Third-Party Beneficiaries; 10.11 Headings. These Bank Turn 1 provisions remain unchanged, except that “North Carolina” references in the UCC and electronic-execution provisions are conformed to “New York” where they describe contractual governing law.')
heading(red,'Section 11 — Fees and Expenses',1)
revision(red,'11.1 Annual Maintenance Fee.','Depositor shall pay $3,500 per Account per annum, currently $10,500 for three Accounts, payable in advance and debitable from the Operating Account.','Depositor shall pay Bank an annual Account control agreement maintenance fee of $3,500 per Account per annum (currently three Accounts, for a total of $10,500), payable in advance on the Effective Date and each anniversary. This fee may be debited from the Operating Account in accordance with the Account agreements.','Accepted as within market range.')
revision(red,'11.2 Legal-Fee Reimbursement.','Depositor shall reimburse Bank for outside legal costs in an amount equal to $15,000, payable upon execution and debit-able from the Operating Account.','Depositor shall reimburse Bank for documented outside legal costs incurred in connection with review, negotiation and execution of this Agreement, in an amount equal to the lesser of (a) $7,500 and (b) the actual documented fees incurred, payable once upon execution. No additional legal-fee reimbursement shall be payable for future amendments, modifications or supplements unless separately agreed in writing.','Good-faith fee accommodation; preserves proportionality and documentation.')
body(red,'11.3 Priority of Fees. Fees shall not be used to condition Bank’s performance of any obligation under this Agreement, including compliance with a NOEC.')
heading(red,'Section 12 — Representations and Warranties',1)
revision(red,'12.1(b) Exclusive Control; No Other Agreements.','The Accounts are solely in the name of Depositor, and no other person or entity (other than Secured Party) has been granted control over the Accounts.','The Accounts are solely in the name of Depositor, and no other person or entity (other than Secured Party pursuant to this Agreement) has been granted control over the Accounts. Bank has not entered into, and covenants that it will not enter into, any control agreement, blocked-account agreement, escrow agreement or similar arrangement with respect to the Accounts without the prior written consent of Secured Party.','Restores the no-prior-control-agreement representation and covenant.')
revision(red,'12.1(c) No Other Liens or Claims.','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the Bank’s representation regarding other liens and claims.]','Bank has received no notice of any Lien, claim, interest or adverse claim in or with respect to the Accounts other than the security interest of Secured Party and Depositor’s rights as account holder, and Bank is not aware of any pending or threatened claim affecting the Accounts.','Supports first-priority control analysis.')
body(red,'12.1(a), 12.1(d) and 12.1(e) (Organization and Authority, Bank’s Jurisdiction and Enforceability), and Depositor’s representations in Section 12.2, remain as set out in Bank Turn 1, subject to the conforming New York references above.')

Our comments on the Bank’s substantive changes are below.')

heading(cover,'Substantive Responses to Bank Turn 1',1)
items=[('1. Section 2(a) — “Entitlement Order” versus “Instruction” terminology (reject / restore).','We have restored “Entitlement Order” terminology alongside “Instructions” in the operative control provisions and the definition section. Pinnacle’s form uses this dual-track formulation deliberately: “Entitlement Order” preserves the Article 8 control concept if an Account is characterized as, or later deemed to be, a securities account, while “Instruction” preserves the Article 9 deposit-account control mechanism under UCC §9-104(a)(2). The language does not independently characterize an ordinary demand deposit account as a securities account or Ironbridge as a securities intermediary; it simply preserves the Article 8 protection if applicable. This is important to Pinnacle’s perfection analysis and is not intended to impose an operational burden beyond the Bank’s existing agreement to follow Secured Party directions.'),('2. Section 2 — Springing exclusive control and ordinary-course account operation (counter-propose).','We accept the Bank’s concern that Graycliff should be able to operate the Accounts in the ordinary course before a Notice of Exclusive Control (“NOEC”). The counter-markup therefore makes that pre-NOEC permission explicit. The distinction after an NOEC is critical, however: upon Ironbridge’s receipt of an NOEC, the pre-NOEC operating permission terminates immediately, Ironbridge must not accept or process new Depositor Instructions, and exclusive compliance with Pinnacle’s Instructions begins. The Bank’s internal implementation period cannot become a continuing carve-out for Graycliff’s access or a condition to Pinnacle’s control.'),('3. Sections 3–4 — Conflicting instructions and Bank set-off priority (reject / restore).','We have deleted the proposed priority for Ironbridge’s set-off, recoupment and lien rights over Pinnacle’s Instructions. In a control agreement, the waterfall must be clear: where Instructions conflict, Pinnacle’s Instructions and Entitlement Orders prevail, and after an NOEC Ironbridge must comply exclusively with Pinnacle’s Instructions. This structure is central to the UCC control framework and is necessary to ensure that the account-control arrangement works when the Secured Party needs to exercise its remedies.'),('4. Section 4 — Scope of set-off (counter-propose).','As a good-faith accommodation to the Bank’s stated set-off concerns, we have narrowed the permitted set-off carve-out rather than insisting on an absolute prohibition. Ironbridge may exercise set-off only for direct, matured, liquidated and then-due obligations arising directly under the deposit-account agreements relating to these Accounts. The carve-out excludes contingent, disputed, unliquidated or unmatured obligations, derivatives, swaps, foreign exchange, letters of credit, unrelated credit facilities and affiliate obligations. This formulation is intended to address customary account-level charges without permitting unrelated or contingent exposures to prime Pinnacle’s collateral.'),('5. Section 5 — NOEC compliance period (counter at three Business Days).','We have changed the Bank’s five-Business-Day period to three Business Days following Ironbridge’s receipt and authentication of an NOEC. Three Business Days is the maximum period Pinnacle can accept without further approval. It gives the Bank reasonable time to coordinate operations, legal and compliance while limiting the dissipation risk associated with approximately $38.15 million of controlled deposits. The counter-markup also makes clear that no new Depositor debits, withdrawals or transfers may be accepted after the NOEC is received.'),('6. Section 6 — Indemnification for Bank gross negligence (firm rejection).','We have restored the carve-out for losses to the extent arising from Ironbridge’s own gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith. Pinnacle will not indemnify a depository bank for its own gross negligence. This is consistent with standard market practice for control agreements: an indemnity may protect a bank for good-faith performance and compliance with authorized Secured Party directions, but it should not shift the risk of the Bank’s own serious misconduct to the Secured Party.'),('7. Section 7(a) — $50,000 aggregate liability cap (reject / delete).','The $50,000 cap has been deleted in its entirety. The controlled Accounts hold approximately $38.15 million in aggregate. A $50,000 cap is de minimis in relation to the assets Ironbridge is being asked to control and would provide no meaningful accountability or recovery if a Bank breach resulted in the release or loss of controlled funds. Pinnacle therefore cannot accept the proposed cap in its current form.'),('8. Section 7(b) — Consequential, punitive and indirect damages waiver (accept with clarification).','This is a lower-priority commercial point. We have retained a mutual waiver, but clarified that it does not limit either party’s obligations under the indemnification provision or Pinnacle’s right to recover direct damages, including amounts released from an Account in breach of the Agreement. We are not seeking to make this issue a separate impediment, provided the waiver remains mutual and does not operate to limit direct account-balance damages.'),('9. Section 8 — Set-off lookback and subordination of Bank liens (counter at 180 days).','We have changed the Bank’s 90-day lookback to 180 days. Pinnacle’s preferred position remains full subordination of Bank liens and set-off rights, subject only to customary documented account fees and return items. As a negotiated middle ground in this turn, 180 days is the minimum acceptable lookback; a shorter period would leave a material gap in the subordination protection at precisely the time when the Accounts may be most important to the collateral package.'),('10. Section 9 — Termination rights (reject 30 days / counter at 90 days with transition protections).','Pinnacle’s preference is that Ironbridge not have a unilateral termination right while the Credit Agreement obligations remain outstanding. If the Bank requires an exit right, the counter-markup provides for at least 90 days’ prior written notice, continued compliance with the Agreement (including any outstanding NOEC) during the notice period, commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts and a replacement ACA, and no effectiveness of termination until Pinnacle confirms in writing that the replacement ACA has been executed and delivered. Abrupt termination on 30 days’ notice could impair the perfection of Pinnacle’s security interest and create a control gap.'),('11. Section 10 — Governing law and forum (reject North Carolina / restore New York).','We have restored New York governing law and the New York forum. The Credit Agreement and the broader Loan Documents are governed by New York law, and consistency avoids interpretive and choice-of-law complications within the transaction. UCC §9-304 independently governs perfection and priority based on the applicable jurisdiction for the deposit account; selecting New York as the contractual governing law does not displace that mandatory rule. Pinnacle is therefore requesting New York law and the New York courts specified in the counter-markup.'),('12. Section 12 — No prior control agreements and liens (reject deletion / restore).','We have restored Ironbridge’s representations that no other person has been granted control over the Accounts, that Ironbridge has not entered into a competing control, blocked-account, escrow or similar arrangement, and that Ironbridge has received no notice of other Liens, claims or adverse interests except as disclosed in the Agreement. These confirmations are important to Pinnacle’s first-priority control analysis. Section 2(a) — “Entitlement Order” versus “Instruction” terminology (reject / restore).','We have restored “Entitlement Order” terminology alongside “Instructions” in the operative control provisions and the definition section. Pinnacle’s form uses this dual-track formulation deliberately: “Entitlement Order” preserves the Article 8 control concept if an Account is characterized as, or later deemed to be, a securities account, while “Instruction” preserves the Article 9 deposit-account control mechanism under UCC §9-104(a)(2). The language does not independently characterize an ordinary demand deposit account as a securities account or Ironbridge as a securities intermediary; it simply preserves the Article 8 protection if applicable. This is important to Pinnacle’s perfection analysis and is not intended to impose an operational burden beyond the Bank’s existing agreement to follow Secured Party directions.'),('2. Section 2 — Springing exclusive control and ordinary-course account operation (counter-propose).','We accept the Bank’s concern that Graycliff should be able to operate the Accounts in the ordinary course before a Notice of Exclusive Control (“NOEC”). The counter-markup therefore makes that pre-NOEC permission explicit. The distinction after an NOEC is critical, however: upon Ironbridge’s receipt of an NOEC, the pre-NOEC operating permission terminates immediately, Ironbridge must not accept or process new Depositor Instructions, and exclusive compliance with Pinnacle’s Instructions begins. The Bank’s internal implementation period cannot become a continuing carve-out for Graycliff’s access or a condition to Pinnacle’s control.'),('3. Sections 3–4 — Conflicting instructions and Bank set-off priority (reject / restore).','We have deleted the proposed priority for Ironbridge’s set-off, recoupment and lien rights over Pinnacle’s Instructions. In a control agreement, the waterfall must be clear: where Instructions conflict, Pinnacle’s Instructions and Entitlement Orders prevail, and after an NOEC Ironbridge must comply exclusively with Pinnacle’s Instructions. This structure is central to the UCC control framework and is necessary to ensure that the account-control arrangement works when the Secured Party needs to exercise its remedies.'),('4. Section 4 — Scope of set-off (counter-propose).','As a good-faith accommodation to the Bank’s stated set-off concerns, we have narrowed the permitted set-off carve-out rather than insisting on an absolute prohibition. Ironbridge may exercise set-off only for direct, matured, liquidated and then-due obligations arising directly under the deposit-account agreements relating to these Accounts. The carve-out excludes contingent, disputed, unliquidated or unmatured obligations, derivatives, swaps, foreign exchange, letters of credit, unrelated credit facilities and affiliate obligations. This formulation is intended to address customary account-level charges without permitting unrelated or contingent exposures to prime Pinnacle’s collateral.'),('5. Section 5 — NOEC compliance period (counter at three Business Days).','We have changed the Bank’s five-Business-Day period to three Business Days following Ironbridge’s receipt and authentication of an NOEC. Three Business Days is the maximum period Pinnacle can accept without further approval. It gives the Bank reasonable time to coordinate operations, legal and compliance while limiting the dissipation risk associated with approximately $38.15 million of controlled deposits. The counter-markup also makes clear that no new Depositor debits, withdrawals or transfers may be accepted after the NOEC is received.'),('6. Section 6 — Indemnification for Bank gross negligence (firm rejection).','We have restored the carve-out for losses to the extent arising from Ironbridge’s own gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith. Pinnacle will not indemnify a depository bank for its own gross negligence. This is consistent with standard market practice for control agreements: an indemnity may protect a bank for good-faith performance and compliance with authorized Secured Party directions, but it should not shift the risk of the Bank’s own serious misconduct to the Secured Party.'),('7. Section 7(a) — $50,000 aggregate liability cap (reject / delete).','The $50,000 cap has been deleted in its entirety. The controlled Accounts hold approximately $38.15 million in aggregate. Section 7(b) — Consequential, punitive and indirect damages waiver (accept with clarification).','This is a lower-priority commercial point. heading(red,'Parties and Recitals — Agreed Bank Turn 1 Facts',2)
body(red,'This DEPOSIT ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of [DATE], 2025 (the “Effective Date”), by and among Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as secured party (the “Secured Party”); Graycliff Industries, Inc., a Delaware corporation, as depositor/debtor (the “Depositor”); and Ironbridge National Bank, N.A., a national banking association (the “Bank”).')
body(red,'Depositor maintains the Accounts identified on Schedule A. Secured Party has been granted a security interest in the Accounts and the funds therein under the Credit Agreement dated April 14, 2025, maturing April 14, 2030, and the related Loan Documents. The Parties enter into this Agreement to establish control over the Accounts for purposes of perfection under the UCC.')
heading(red,'Section 1 — Definitions',1)
body(red,'“Account” means each deposit account identified on Schedule A, including renewals, replacements, reclassifications, redesignations and successor accounts, and all funds and proceeds credited thereto.')
body(red,'“Business Day” means a day on which Bank is open for substantially all commercial banking business at its offices in Charlotte, North Carolina, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and days on which banking institutions in North Carolina are authorized or required to close.')
revision(red,'“Entitlement Order.”','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the definition of “Entitlement Order” and used “Instructions” only in the operative control provisions.]','“Entitlement Order” has the meaning assigned to that term in UCC §8-102(a)(8) and includes any notification communicated to Bank directing the transfer, redemption, liquidation or other disposition of a financial asset or interest therein, including any instruction originated by Secured Party pursuant to this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, the use of “Entitlement Order” does not, by itself, characterize any Account as a securities account or Bank as a securities intermediary.','Restores Article 8 term on a conditional, belt-and-suspenders basis.')
body(red,'“Event of Default,” “Notice of Exclusive Control” or “NOEC,” “Instructions,” “Lien,” “Loan Documents,” and “UCC” have the meanings assigned in the Bank Turn 1 document, except that references to the UCC shall be read consistently with the New York governing-law and applicable-jurisdiction provisions below.')
heading(red,'Section 2 — The Accounts; Establishment of Control',1)
body(red,'2.1 Confirmation of Accounts. Bank confirms that each Account listed on Schedule A is maintained at Bank, is held in the name of Depositor, and constitutes a “deposit account” within the meaning of the UCC. Bank is the “bank” within the meaning of UCC §9-102(a)(8) with respect to each Account.')
revision(red,'2.2 Establishment of Control.','Bank hereby agrees that, from and after the Effective Date, it will comply with Instructions originated by Secured Party directing the disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent of Depositor, thereby establishing control under UCC §9-104(a)(2).','Bank hereby agrees that, from and after the Effective Date, it will comply with Entitlement Orders and Instructions originated by Secured Party directing the disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent of Depositor, thereby establishing control by Secured Party over the Accounts within the meaning of UCC §§9-104(a)(2) and 8-106, to the extent applicable. Bank’s compliance obligation is unconditional and is not subject to any condition precedent other than delivery in accordance with the notice and authentication provisions of this Agreement.','Restores dual-track control language without requiring Depositor consent.')
body(red,'2.3 No Changes to Accounts Without Consent. Bank shall not, without the prior written consent of Secured Party, change the name, account number, title, designation or ownership of an Account; close, terminate or redesignate an Account; open an Account intended to be subject to this Agreement; merge or combine an Account; or permit a change to authorized signatories objected to in writing by Secured Party.')
body(red,'2.4 Depositor’s Consent. Depositor irrevocably authorizes and consents to Bank’s compliance with all Instructions and Entitlement Orders originated by Secured Party, without inquiry into Secured Party’s authority and without notice to Depositor. Depositor acknowledges that Bank shall have no liability to Depositor for complying in accordance with this Agreement.')
revision(red,'2.5 Depositor’s Operating Rights Prior to Notice of Exclusive Control.','Unless and until Bank has received a Notice of Exclusive Control, Depositor shall have the full and unrestricted right to issue Instructions with respect to the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, without consent or notification to Secured Party.','Prior to Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Depositor may operate the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, including withdrawals, transfers, payments, ACH transactions and other customary banking transactions, without prior consent of Secured Party. This ordinary-course permission terminates immediately upon Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control; after that receipt, Bank shall not accept or process any new Depositor Instruction, and Depositor shall have no right to withdraw funds or give Instructions with respect to the Accounts.','Preserves the Bank’s operational concern only before NOEC; no post-NOEC carve-out.')
heading(red,'Section 3 — Exclusive Control Upon Notice of Exclusive Control',1)
revision(red,'3.1 Effect of Notice of Exclusive Control.','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the former Section 3 and replaced it with Bank Priority / Set-Off Rights.]','Upon Bank’s receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control delivered in accordance with Section 10: (a) Bank shall immediately cease complying with all Instructions originated by or on behalf of Depositor and shall reject, refuse to honor and return unpaid any Depositor payment order presented or received after such receipt; (b) Bank shall comply solely and exclusively with Instructions and Entitlement Orders originated by or on behalf of Secured Party, including transfers, withdrawals, account closing and delivery of statements; (c) Bank shall freeze and block all automated or preauthorized debits and recurring transactions originated by Depositor; and (d) Bank shall provide Secured Party with current balance and transaction information promptly upon request. Bank shall not require Depositor consent, approval, confirmation or other authorization as a condition to compliance.','Restores springing exclusive control and makes the post-NOEC cutoff unconditional.')
body(red,'3.2 No Requirement of Proof. Bank shall not require evidence of an Event of Default, a court order, judgment, Depositor certificate or other documentation as a condition to compliance with a NOEC. Bank’s sole obligation is to verify that the NOEC is written, purports to come from Secured Party or its authorized representative, is delivered in accordance with Section 10, and directs exclusive compliance with Secured Party’s Instructions.')
body(red,'3.3 Rescission. A NOEC remains in effect until Secured Party delivers a written rescission notice. Upon receipt of a rescission notice, Section 2.5 shall again apply. Bank shall comply with a rescission notice within two (2) Business Days.')
heading(red,'Section 4 — Conflicting Instructions; Waterfall',1)
revision(red,'4.1 Priority of Instructions.','Bank’s rights of set-off, recoupment, banker’s lien and security interest shall at all times be prior and superior to Instructions received from Secured Party.','In the event of a conflict between Instructions or Entitlement Orders received from Secured Party and Instructions received from Depositor, the Instructions and Entitlement Orders of Secured Party shall control and prevail at all times, whether or not a NOEC has been delivered. Bank shall comply immediately with Secured Party’s Instructions and shall not give priority to any inconsistent Depositor Instruction. After receipt of a NOEC, Bank shall comply exclusively with Secured Party’s Instructions and shall not be required to follow any Depositor Instruction.','Rejects Bank priority; Secured Party control is the agreed waterfall.')
revision(red,'4.2 Notice of Conflicts.','Bank shall have no liability to Secured Party for complying with Bank’s own rights in priority to Secured Party’s Instructions.','Bank shall promptly, and in any event within one (1) Business Day, notify Secured Party in writing of any conflicting or potentially conflicting Depositor Instruction and shall await further direction from Secured Party before acting on that Instruction, except to the extent delay would violate applicable law.','Provides visibility without granting Bank discretion to override Secured Party.')
heading(red,'Section 5 — Set-Off Scope and NOEC Compliance Period',1)
revision(red,'5.1 Permitted Set-Off Scope.','Bank reserves and retains the unrestricted right to set off, charge, debit or apply funds against any obligation owed to Bank by Depositor, whether direct or contingent, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, and whether or not related to the Accounts.','Subject to Sections 4 and 8, Bank may exercise set-off only with respect to obligations of Depositor to Bank that are (a) direct, (b) matured, liquidated and then due and payable, and (c) arising directly under deposit account agreements between Bank and Depositor relating to the Accounts. Bank shall not exercise set-off for any contingent, disputed, unliquidated or unmatured obligation, any obligation arising under a derivative, swap, foreign exchange, letter-of-credit, credit facility or other unrelated agreement, or any obligation owed to an affiliate of Bank.','Good-faith accommodation; excludes contingent and unrelated exposures.')
body(red,'5.2 No Prior Notice or Consent Required. Bank may exercise a permitted set-off without prior notice to or consent of Secured Party, subject to the scope and priority limitations in this Agreement and the Bank’s obligation to notify Secured Party promptly after exercise.')
revision(red,'5.3 NOEC Compliance Period.','Bank shall comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control within five (5) Business Days of receipt thereof.','Bank shall comply with a Notice of Exclusive Control beginning no later than the third (3rd) Business Day following Bank’s receipt and authentication of the Notice of Exclusive Control. During that period, Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement the NOEC as promptly as practicable and shall not permit new debits, withdrawals or transfers initiated by Depositor after Bank’s receipt of the NOEC.','Three Business Days is the maximum client-approved period.')
heading(red,'Section 6 — Indemnification',1)
revision(red,'6.1–6.2 Secured Party Indemnification.','The indemnification obligations of Secured Party shall apply regardless of whether Losses arise in whole or in part from the negligence (including gross negligence) of Bank, and shall be limited only where Losses are determined to have resulted solely and directly from Bank’s willful misconduct.','The Depositor and Secured Party, jointly and severally, shall indemnify and hold harmless Bank and its officers, directors, employees and agents from claims, losses, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising out of Bank’s performance of its obligations or compliance with Secured Party’s Instructions; provided, however, that the indemnification shall not extend to claims, losses, liabilities, costs or expenses to the extent arising from Bank’s own gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith.','Restores the market-standard gross-negligence, willful-misconduct and bad-faith carve-out.')
body(red,'6.3 Depositor Indemnification. Depositor’s indemnity for its breach, inaccurate representations and third-party claims remains as set out in Bank Turn 1, subject to the foregoing carve-out for Bank conduct.')
heading(red,'Section 7 — Limitation of Liability',1)
revision(red,'7.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.','Bank’s aggregate liability under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000). The limitation shall not apply only to Losses resulting from Bank’s willful misconduct.','[DELETED IN FULL — NO AGGREGATE LIABILITY CAP.]','The proposed cap is deleted; the controlled deposits total approximately $38.15 million.')
revision(red,'7.2 Consequential Damages.','NO PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO ANY OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES OF ANY KIND WHATSOEVER, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT, NEGLIGENCE, STRICT LIABILITY OR ANY OTHER THEORY, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY.','No party shall be liable to any other party for any indirect, consequential, special, punitive or exemplary damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement, regardless of the form of action or theory of liability; provided that this Section shall not limit the obligations of Depositor or Secured Party under Section 6 or limit recovery of direct damages, including amounts released from an Account in breach of this Agreement.','Mutual waiver accepted on a clarified basis; direct account-balance damages and indemnity remain available.')
body(red,'7.3 No Duty to Monitor; 7.4 Good Faith Reliance; 7.5 No Fiduciary Duty. These Bank Turn 1 provisions remain unchanged, except that good-faith reliance does not excuse a breach caused by Bank’s gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith.')
heading(red,'Section 8 — Subordination of Bank Liens; Waiver of Set-Off',1)
revision(red,'8.1 Limited Subordination / Lookback Period.','Bank agrees to subordinate its Liens solely to the extent of fees, charges and returned items accrued or incurred during the ninety (90) day period immediately preceding delivery of a NOEC, and Liens arising before that period or after delivery of the NOEC remain prior and superior.','Bank shall subordinate its Liens, security interests, claims, counterclaims and rights of set-off in the Accounts and funds therein to the security interest of Secured Party; provided that, as a negotiated accommodation, Bank may retain the limited rights described in Section 5.1 only for obligations arising during the one hundred eighty (180) day period immediately preceding delivery of a NOEC. No Bank Lien or set-off right for a period shorter than one hundred eighty (180) days, or for a post-NOEC obligation other than customary documented account fees and return items, shall be prior to Secured Party’s security interest.','Counters the 90-day period at the client-directed 180-day minimum.')
body(red,'8.2 Fee and Return-Item Exceptions. Bank may debit customary, documented maintenance fees, service charges and return items directly attributable to the Accounts in accordance with the agreed fee schedule, but such charges shall not be used to defeat Secured Party’s control or priority.')
heading(red,'Section 9 — Successor Bank; Termination',1)
revision(red,'Section 9 heading and successor provisions.','Section 9 — [DELETED: Successor Bank; Notification Obligations] [ADDED: Termination]','Section 9 — Successor Bank; Notification Obligations; Termination','Restores successor-bank continuity and keeps the Bank’s termination request subject to transition protections.')
revision(red,'9.1 Successor Bank Notification.','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the successor-bank notification obligation in its entirety.]','Bank shall provide Secured Party at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice of any proposed merger, consolidation, assignment, transfer of the Accounts, change of charter or other succession event that would result in a successor bank holding the Accounts. Any successor bank shall be bound by this Agreement, and Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a written assumption of Bank’s obligations; provided that the notice obligation applies to the extent legally permissible.','Thirty days’ prior written notice is required to maintain visibility and continuity.')
body(red,'9.2 Termination by Secured Party; 9.3 No Unilateral Termination by Depositor. The Bank Turn 1 provisions remain unchanged.')
revision(red,'9.4 Bank Termination.','Bank may terminate this Agreement, in its sole discretion, upon thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, without any requirement that a successor bank be appointed or a replacement agreement executed.','Bank may terminate this Agreement only upon not less than ninety (90) days’ prior written notice to Secured Party and Depositor; provided that (i) during the notice period Bank shall continue to comply with all obligations hereunder, including any outstanding NOEC, (ii) Depositor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts at a depository bank reasonably acceptable to Secured Party and deliver a replacement ACA reasonably satisfactory to Secured Party, and (iii) this Agreement shall not terminate until Secured Party confirms in writing that the replacement ACA has been executed and delivered. Bank shall cooperate with the transition and provide account statements and transaction information reasonably requested by Secured Party.','Fallback transition language; prevents a perfection gap.')
heading(red,'Section 10 — Notices; Governing Law; Jurisdiction; Miscellaneous',1)
body(red,'10.1 Notices. The Bank Turn 1 notice methods, notice addresses and authentication procedures remain unchanged, with the Account contacts and addresses shown in the Bank Turn 1 document.')
revision(red,'10.2 Governing Law.','This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles.','This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and interpreted in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles thereof that would require or permit application of the laws of another jurisdiction. Matters relating to perfection, priority and enforcement of security interests in the Accounts shall be determined under the UCC as in effect in the applicable jurisdiction under UCC §9-304.','Restores consistency with the Credit Agreement and Loan Documents.')
revision(red,'10.3 Jurisdiction; Venue.','Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina.','Each Party irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York and the Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York, and the appellate courts thereof, for any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement.','Restores the New York forum selected in Pinnacle’s form.')
body(red,'10.4 Waiver of Jury Trial; 10.5 Amendments; 10.6 Entire Agreement; 10.7 Severability; 10.8 Counterparts and Electronic Execution; 10.9 Successors and Assigns; 10.10 No Third-Party Beneficiaries; 10.11 Headings. These Bank Turn 1 provisions remain unchanged, except that “North Carolina” references in the UCC and electronic-execution provisions are conformed to “New York” where they describe contractual governing law.')
heading(red,'Section 11 — Fees and Expenses',1)
revision(red,'11.1 Annual Maintenance Fee.','Depositor shall pay $3,500 per Account per annum, currently $10,500 for three Accounts, payable in advance and debitable from the Operating Account.','Depositor shall pay Bank an annual Account control agreement maintenance fee of $3,500 per Account per annum (currently three Accounts, for a total of $10,500), payable in advance on the Effective Date and each anniversary. This fee may be debited from the Operating Account in accordance with the Account agreements.','Accepted as within market range.')
revision(red,'11.2 Legal-Fee Reimbursement.','Depositor shall reimburse Bank for outside legal costs in an amount equal to $15,000, payable upon execution and debit-able from the Operating Account.','Depositor shall reimburse Bank for documented outside legal costs incurred in connection with review, negotiation and execution of this Agreement, in an amount equal to the lesser of (a) $7,500 and (b) the actual documented fees incurred, payable once upon execution. No additional legal-fee reimbursement shall be payable for future amendments, modifications or supplements unless separately agreed in writing.','Good-faith fee accommodation; preserves proportionality and documentation.')
body(red,'11.3 Priority of Fees. Fees shall not be used to condition Bank’s performance of any obligation under this Agreement, including compliance with a NOEC.')
heading(red,'Section 12 — Representations and Warranties',1)
revision(red,'12.1(b) Exclusive Control; No Other Agreements.','The Accounts are solely in the name of Depositor, and no other person or entity (other than Secured Party) has been granted control over the Accounts.','The Accounts are solely in the name of Depositor, and no other person or entity (other than Secured Party pursuant to this Agreement) has been granted control over the Accounts. Bank has not entered into, and covenants that it will not enter into, any control agreement, blocked-account agreement, escrow agreement or similar arrangement with respect to the Accounts without the prior written consent of Secured Party.','Restores the no-prior-control-agreement representation and covenant.')
revision(red,'12.1(c) No Other Liens or Claims.','[Bank Turn 1 deleted the Bank’s representation regarding other liens and claims.]','Bank has received no notice of any Lien, claim, interest or adverse claim in or with respect to the Accounts other than the security interest of Secured Party and Depositor’s rights as account holder, and Bank is not aware of any pending or threatened claim affecting the Accounts.','Supports first-priority control analysis.')
body(red,'12.1(a), 12.1(d) and 12.1(e) (Organization and Authority, Bank’s Jurisdiction and Enforceability), and Depositor’s representations in Section 12.2, remain as set out in Bank Turn 1, subject to the conforming New York references above.')

heading(cover,'Substantive Responses to Bank Turn 1',1)
items=[('1. Section 2(a) — “Entitlement Order” versus “Instruction” terminology (reject / restore).','We have restored “Entitlement Order” terminology alongside “Instructions” in the operative control provisions and the definition section. Pinnacle’s form uses this dual-track formulation deliberately: “Entitlement Order” preserves the Article 8 control concept if an Account is characterized as, or later deemed to be, a securities account, while “Instruction” preserves the Article 9 deposit-account control mechanism under UCC §9-104(a)(2). The language does not independently characterize an ordinary demand deposit account as a securities account or Ironbridge as a securities intermediary; it simply preserves the Article 8 protection if applicable. This is important to Pinnacle’s perfection analysis and is not intended to impose an operational burden beyond the Bank’s existing agreement to follow Secured Party directions.'),('2. Section 2 — Springing exclusive control and ordinary-course account operation (counter-propose).','We accept the Bank’s concern that Graycliff should be able to operate the Accounts in the ordinary course before a Notice of Exclusive Control (“NOEC”). The counter-markup therefore makes that pre-NOEC permission explicit. The distinction after an NOEC is critical, however: upon Ironbridge’s receipt of an NOEC, the pre-NOEC operating permission terminates immediately, Ironbridge must not accept or process new Depositor Instructions, and exclusive compliance with Pinnacle’s Instructions begins. The Bank’s internal implementation period cannot become a continuing carve-out for Graycliff’s access or a condition to Pinnacle’s control.'),('3. Sections 3–4 — Conflicting instructions and Bank set-off priority (reject / restore).','We have deleted the proposed priority for Ironbridge’s set-off, recoupment and lien rights over Pinnacle’s Instructions. In a control agreement, the waterfall must be clear: where Instructions conflict, Pinnacle’s Instructions and Entitlement Orders prevail, and after an NOEC Ironbridge must comply exclusively with Pinnacle’s Instructions. This structure is central to the UCC control framework and is necessary to ensure that the account-control arrangement works when the Secured Party needs to exercise its remedies.'),('4. Section 4 — Scope of set-off (counter-propose).','As a good-faith accommodation to the Bank’s stated set-off concerns, we have narrowed the permitted set-off carve-out rather than insisting on an absolute prohibition. Ironbridge may exercise set-off only for direct, matured, liquidated and then-due obligations arising directly under the deposit-account agreements relating to these Accounts. The carve-out excludes contingent, disputed, unliquidated or unmatured obligations, derivatives, swaps, foreign exchange, letters of credit, unrelated credit facilities and affiliate obligations. This formulation is intended to address customary account-level charges without permitting unrelated or contingent exposures to prime Pinnacle’s collateral.'),('5. Section 5 — NOEC compliance period (counter at three Business Days).','We have changed the Bank’s five-Business-Day period to three Business Days following Ironbridge’s receipt and authentication of an NOEC. Three Business Days is the maximum period Pinnacle can accept without further approval. It gives the Bank reasonable time to coordinate operations, legal and compliance while limiting the dissipation risk associated with approximately $38.15 million of controlled deposits. The counter-markup also makes clear that no new Depositor debits, withdrawals or transfers may be accepted after the NOEC is received.'),('6. Section 6 — Indemnification for Bank gross negligence (firm rejection).','We have restored the carve-out for losses to the extent arising from Ironbridge’s own gross negligence, willful misconduct or bad faith. Pinnacle will not indemnify a depository bank for its own gross negligence. This is consistent with standard market practice for control agreements: an indemnity may protect a bank for good-faith performance and compliance with authorized Secured Party directions, but it should not shift the risk of the Bank’s own serious misconduct to the Secured Party.'),('7. Section 7(a) — $50,000 aggregate liability cap (reject / delete).','The $50,000 cap has been deleted in its entirety. The controlled Accounts hold approximately $38.15 million in aggregate. A $50,000 cap is de minimis in relation to the assets Ironbridge is being asked to control and would provide no meaningful accountability or recovery if a Bank breach resulted in the release or loss of controlled funds. Pinnacle therefore cannot accept the proposed cap in its current form.'),('8. Section 7(b) — Consequential, punitive and indirect damages waiver (accept with clarification).','This is a lower-priority commercial point. We have retained a mutual waiver, but clarified that it does not limit either party’s obligations under the indemnification provision or Pinnacle’s right to recover direct damages, including amounts released from an Account in breach of the Agreement. We are not seeking to make this issue a separate impediment, provided the waiver remains mutual and does not operate to limit direct account-balance damages.'),('9. Section 8 — Set-off lookback and subordination of Bank liens (counter at 180 days).','We have changed the Bank’s 90-day lookback to 180 days. Pinnacle’s preferred position remains full subordination of Bank liens and set-off rights, subject only to customary documented account fees and return items. As a negotiated middle ground in this turn, 180 days is the minimum acceptable lookback; a shorter period would leave a material gap in the subordination protection at precisely the time when the Accounts may be most important to the collateral package.'),('10. Section 9 — Termination rights (reject 30 days / counter at 90 days with transition protections).','Pinnacle’s preference is that Ironbridge not have a unilateral termination right while the Credit Agreement obligations remain outstanding. If the Bank requires an exit right, the counter-markup provides for at least 90 days’ prior written notice, continued compliance with the Agreement (including any outstanding NOEC) during the notice period, commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts and a replacement ACA, and no effectiveness of termination until Pinnacle confirms in writing that the replacement ACA has been executed and delivered. Abrupt termination on 30 days’ notice could impair the perfection of Pinnacle’s security interest and create a control gap.'),('11. Section 10 — Governing law and forum (reject North Carolina / restore New York).','We have restored New York governing law and the New York forum. The Credit Agreement and the broader Loan Documents are governed by New York law, and consistency avoids interpretive and choice-of-law complications within the transaction. UCC §9-304 independently governs perfection and priority based on the applicable jurisdiction for the deposit account; selecting New York as the contractual governing law does not displace that mandatory rule. Pinnacle is therefore requesting New York law and the New York courts specified in the counter-markup.'),('12. Section 12 — No prior control agreements and liens (reject deletion / restore).','We have restored Ironbridge’s representations that no other person has been granted control over the Accounts, that Ironbridge has not entered into a competing control, blocked-account, escrow or similar arrangement, and that Ironbridge has received no notice of other Liens, claims or adverse interests except as disclosed in the Agreement. These confirmations are important to Pinnacle’s first-priority control analysis. A public UCC search will not reveal a competing control agreement, so the Bank’s representation is an important part of the perfection and priority diligence.'),('13. Successor-bank notification (reject deletion / restore).','We have restored a requirement that Ironbridge provide at least 30 days’ prior written notice of any merger, consolidation, transfer of the Accounts, change of charter or other succession event that would place the Accounts with a successor bank, to the extent legally permissible. We also ask that Ironbridge use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a written assumption of the ACA. The notice obligation is necessary to preserve visibility and allow the parties to arrange a replacement or confirm continuity of control before a transfer occurs.')]
